### Reproduced on the published packages

Tested official `pm-context@2026.11.19` and `@unbrained/pm-cli@2026.11.19`, Node 24.22.3, in disposable no-Git trackers. The [shipped README](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/v2026.11.19/README.md#L226-L230) promises repeated and comma-separated citation values and refusal of the whole submission on any unknown citation.

Create two synthetic tasks and run `pm context-pack --ids "$ITEM_A,$ITEM_B" --format json`. Use the receipt ID `R` and any two distinct served fact IDs `A` and `B` from that receipt. Use a fresh equivalent receipt for each invocation so recorded usage cannot affect the comparison.

| Arguments after `pm context-usage --receipt "$R"` | Exit | Used / cited facts |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `--cite "$A" --cite "$B" --json` | 0 | 1 / 1 |
| `--cite "$A,$B" --json` | 0 | 2 / 2 |
| `--cite unserved-synthetic-fact --cite "$B" --json` | 0 | 1 / 1 |
| `--cite "unserved-synthetic-fact,$B" --json` | 2 | Refused |

This undercounts context actually used and lets a preceding unknown ID disappear instead of rejecting the submission. **Workaround:** use one comma-separated `--cite` value.

The [released command declaration](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/blob/v2026.11.19/index.ts#L1874) documents repetition but declares a scalar string. The SDK-array refusal in the open dependency [PR #240](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-context/pull/240) is consistent with that mismatch, but the native defect was independently reproduced on published artifacts. Adjacent `--touch` and `--edited-file` repeat behavior was not tested here.

### Acceptance

- Repeated and comma-separated citations preserve the same complete set, including via a supported SDK invocation, without counting duplicate IDs twice.
- An unknown value in any position refuses the whole submission without recording usage or mutating item/history data.
- Check the documented repeated forms on the adjacent options; preserve native argument validation and receipt boundaries.
context-usage silently drops earlier repeated --cite values
